title: Bucko–Czap conjecture on 1-planarity of lexicographic products
statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $K_2$ denote the complete graph with two vertices. A graph is **1-planar** if it has a drawing in the plane in which every edge is crossed by at most one other edge. A **cactus** is a connected graph in which every edge belongs to at most one cycle. **Bucko–Czap's conjecture.** The graph $G\circ K_2$ is 1-planar if and only if $G$ is a cactus. This open problem characterizes 1-planarity for lexicographic products with $K_2$ and concerns the relationship between graph substitution and sparse crossing structures.
source_name: Licheng Zhang and Yuanqiu Huang, “The reducibility of optimal 1-planar graphs”, arXiv:2211.14733 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14733

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2022). “So the study of 1-planarity of the lexicographic products of graphs only leaves the following open problem.”
